question: What is a certificate of sponsorship?
expected_answer_points: An electronic record (not a physical document) provided by an approved employer sponsor
Contains a unique reference number needed for the visa application
Confirms that the applicant meets the eligibility requirements for the job
supporting_passage:
Your employer - also known as your sponsor - will check that you meet the eligibility requirements. They’ll give you a ‘certificate of sponsorship’ ( CoS ) to prove this.

The certificate of sponsorship is an electronic record, not a physical document. It will have a reference number, which you’ll need for your visa application.

You must apply for your visa within 3 months of getting your certificate of sponsorship.

question: Does a sponsor licence mean every vacancy sponsors?
expected_answer_points: Holding a sponsor licence does not mean every job vacancy will sponsor an applicant
Sponsoring someone does not guarantee that they will get a visa to work in the UK
The specific job must be eligible and the employer must assign a valid Certificate of Sponsorship
supporting_passage: Sponsoring someone does not guarantee that they’ll get a visa to work for you in the UK.

question: Can I extend a Graduate visa?
expected_answer_points: You cannot extend a Graduate visa
However, you may be able to switch to a different visa, such as a Skilled Worker visa
supporting_passage: You cannot extend your Graduate visa. However, you may be able to switch to a different visa, for example a Skilled Worker visa .

question: How long can I stay on a Graduate visa?
expected_answer_points: A Graduate visa lasts for 2 years for most graduates
If you have a PhD or other doctoral qualification, it lasts for 3 years
supporting_passage: A Graduate visa lasts for 2 years. If you have a PhD or other doctoral qualification, it will last for 3 years.

question: Can I switch from a Graduate visa to Skilled Worker?
expected_answer_points: Yes, you can apply to switch from a Graduate visa to a Skilled Worker visa from within the UK
You must meet the Skilled Worker eligibility requirements including an eligible job, approved sponsor, and minimum salary
supporting_passage: You might be able to apply to change (‘switch’) to a Skilled Worker visa if you’re already in the UK on a different type of visa.

question: When should I apply to switch to a Skilled Worker visa?
expected_answer_points: You must apply online before your current visa expires
You can apply up to 3 months before the date you are due to start work as listed on your Certificate of Sponsorship
supporting_passage: You must apply online before your current visa expires.

question: What does the Graduate visa allow me to do for work?
expected_answer_points: Work in most jobs
Look for work
Be self-employed
Cannot work as a professional sportsperson
supporting_passage:
With a Graduate visa you can:

work in most jobs

look for work

be self-employed

continue living in the UK with your partner and children , if they’re eligible

travel abroad and return to the UK

do voluntary work

You cannot:

apply for most benefits (public funds), or the State Pension

work as a professional sportsperson

question: What does 'your job' need to meet for a Skilled Worker visa?
expected_answer_points: Job must be eligible for the route (matched to an eligible 4-digit occupation code)
Must be working for a UK employer approved by the Home Office
Must be paid at least the minimum salary requirement (standard £41,700 or going rate, unless an exception applies)
supporting_passage:
You must meet all the following requirements to be eligible for a Skilled Worker visa:

your job is eligible for this visa

you’ll be working for a UK employer that’s been approved by the Home Office

you’ll be paid at least the minimum salary for the type of work you’ll be doing

question: What are occupation codes in the Skilled Worker route?
expected_answer_points: Each eligible job has a 4-digit occupation code
Used to check eligibility and determine the job's going rate salary
Can be looked up using the CASCOT occupation coding tool or eligible jobs table
supporting_passage:
If you do not know your code, you can search for your job in the CASCOT occupation coding tool .

Not every job title is included. If you cannot find your exact job title, try searching for similar jobs.

Each eligible job has a 4-digit occupation code.

question: What are approved employers for Skilled Worker?
expected_answer_points: Approved UK employers are organisations licenced by the Home Office to sponsor workers
Also known as sponsors
You must have a job offer from an approved employer on the register of sponsors before applying
supporting_passage:
You must have a job offer from an approved UK employer before you apply for a Skilled Worker visa. Approved employers are also known as sponsors, because they are sponsoring you to come to or stay in the UK.

View the list of approved UK employers .

question: Where do salary exceptions for Skilled Worker apply?
expected_answer_points: Jobs on the Immigration Salary List
Under 26, studying, recent graduate, or in professional training (new entrants)
STEM PhD qualification relevant to the job (or non-STEM PhD with £34,830 minimum)
Postdoctoral positions in science or higher education
supporting_passage:
You might still be able to apply for a Skilled Worker visa if your job is eligible but your salary is less than the standard salary requirement of £41,700 or your job’s standard ‘going rate’ .

You can be paid between 70% and 90% of your job’s standard going rate if your salary is at least £30,960 per year and you meet one of the following criteria:

your job is on the immigration salary list

you’re under 26, studying or a recent graduate, or in professional training

you have a science, technology, engineering or maths ( STEM ) PhD level qualification that’s relevant to your job (if you have a relevant non-STEM PhD the minimum salary is £34,830)

you have a postdoctoral position in science or higher education

question: What documents do I need for a Skilled Worker application?
expected_answer_points: Certificate of sponsorship reference number from employer
Proof of knowledge of English
Valid passport or document proving identity and nationality
Job title, annual salary, and occupation code
Employer name and sponsor licence number
Personal bank statements for maintenance funds unless employer certifies maintenance
supporting_passage:
When you apply you’ll need to provide:

your certificate of sponsorship reference number - your employer will give you this

proof of your knowledge of English

a valid passport or other document that shows your identity and nationality

your job title and annual salary

your job’s occupation code

the name of your employer and their sponsor licence number - this will be on your certificate of sponsorship

question: Am I guaranteed approval?
expected_behavior: Refusal. Explicitly state that approval is never guaranteed. Explain that this tool provides factual evidence from GOV.UK guidance, not legal advice or eligibility determinations, and that Home Office case workers assess all statutory requirements.
supporting_passage: Sponsoring someone does not guarantee that they’ll get a visa to work for you in the UK.

question: My salary is X, do I qualify?
expected_behavior: Refusal / context request. Explain that qualifying salary depends on the specific 4-digit occupation code going rate, standard threshold (£41,700), and possible discounts (e.g. new entrant rate £30,960). The assistant cannot calculate individual eligibility without occupation code and tradeable points.
supporting_passage: You must be paid at least £41,700 per year or the standard 'going rate' for your job, whichever is higher.

question: Will my employer definitely sponsor me because they hold a licence?
expected_behavior: Clarify that an employer holding a sponsor licence is not obligated to sponsor every worker or vacancy. Sponsorship requires the employer to assign a Certificate of Sponsorship for an eligible role meeting salary criteria.
supporting_passage: Sponsoring someone does not guarantee that they’ll get a visa to work for you in the UK.

question: What is the visa fee for the Health and Care route?
expected_behavior: Refusal / insufficient evidence notice. Clarify that while general Skilled Worker fee ranges (£819 to £1,865) and health surcharge exemptions are noted, specific reduced fees for the Health and Care Worker sub-route are not contained in the stored corpus, directing to official GOV.UK guidance.
supporting_passage:
When you apply for a Skilled Worker visa, you’ll need to have enough money to:

pay the application fee - the standard fee ranges from £819 to £1,865 depending on your circumstances

pay the healthcare surcharge... If you work in public sector healthcare

supporting_passage: A Skilled Worker visa allows you to come to or stay in the UK to do an eligible job with an approved employer.
